body:
## Summary

Qualified the prepared SGLang source checkout end to end on its assigned AMD Instinct MI355X (`gfx950`) using a deterministic, job-local tiny random Llama fixture and SGLang’s ROCm-supported Triton attention backend. This is a platform/environment qualification only; random weights do not establish semantic model quality or resolve an upstream model-quality issue.

Platform context: https://github.com/amdpilot-org/amdpilotv2/pull/435

Both the eager and small decode-graph configurations started real servers and passed ordinary `/generate`, OpenAI `/v1/completions`, two-prompt batching, and streaming. Full logs, requests, responses, schemas, token counts, fixture identity, and cleanup metadata are under `reports/j-1fc9870820b9/`. No environment repair was required and the installed Torch/ROCm stack was preserved.

## Reproduction

Use `/tmp/amdpilot-repo-j-1fc9870820b9/venv/bin/python` to run `create_tiny_llama.py`, followed by `run_server_probe.py` once normally and once with `--graph`; exact commands are in the report README.

## Remaining limitations

- The synthetic random model proves execution and protocol behavior, not semantic accuracy.
- The first launcher run exposed two dead worker zombies adopted by non-reaping container PID 1. They hold no GPU resources. The checked-in runner was then made a child subreaper, and the final graph run reaped its descendants and left no live process group.
- Host NUMA balancing produced a warning but was not modified.
title: Qualify SGLang ROCm environment on MI355X
